title: Ten Weeks and One Wrong Year
subtitle: 时间与日程 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 时间与日程（生活与学习·时间与日期）
meta: 主题语境：时间与日程（生活与学习·时间与日期）　|　核心词汇：date　|　正文 338 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 date 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 the clerk ① fixed a date that no office in the town would have confirmed, and he said the fixing was the whole of the notice. The ② date, meaning the day and not the appointment, ran ten weeks and stayed unconfirmed in the register; a date, he said, is the only thing in a register that is judged by how long it is left unentered.

Every ③ date in that register had the same wrong year against it, and the ④ date at the end, meaning the one they kept for the hearing and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever queried twice. A date, his assistant said, is nine parts checking and one part somebody willing to fix; the clerk said the fixing is the part that fills ten weeks.

My aunt meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the date was the whole of the summer, meaning the appointment and not the day. The ⑥ date, meaning the appointment and not any of that, is the only thing in a summer that everybody arranges and nobody keeps; date, she said, is either something you fix or the only word that means both a day and an appointment. She said the appointment is the part they remember.

By 1966 the ⑦ date had become a line in a calendar, and the calendar had become an argument about the wrong year. The ⑧ date of the whole thing, the clerk wrote in March, was one register and ten weeks of fixing; date, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to check. She said the checking was never mentioned.

The ⑨ date I remember is the one at the end, which was kept in 1978 and is still described as the strangest in the register. A ⑩ date, my aunt said in 1980, is the only thing that improves by being kept; every date, she said, is an appointment that has agreed to look like a day. She said the appointment was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 日期；日子（指登记簿上写着的那个）
B. n. 日期（指那一天本身，与那个约会相对）
C. 固定搭配：fix a date 确定一个日期
D. n. 日期（指留给听证会用的那一个）
E. n. 日期；时日（抽象总称，指一本登记簿上的全部日子）
F. n. 日期（指日历上写到、被圈出的那一个）
G. n. 约会；会面（指夏日里安排的那一次）
H. n. 约会（抽象总称，指人人安排却无人守约的那一次）

items.q: fixed a date that no office in the town would have confirmed
The date, meaning the day and not the appointment
the date was the whole of the summer
the date had become a line in a calendar
The date of the whole thing
A date, my aunt said in 1980

answers.why: fix a date 意为“确定一个日期”，1959 年办事员确定了一个全镇没有一家事务所肯确认的日期。
date 意为“日期”，指那一天本身而不是那个约会，它在登记簿上搁了十个星期而未被确认。
date 意为“日期”，指那本登记簿上每一个日期，每一个都有同一个错误的年份对着它。
date 意为“日期”，指留给听证会用的那一个，是唯一有人查问过两次的。
date 意为“约会、会面”，指夏日里安排的那一次，姑姑说这次约会就是那个夏天的全部。
date 意为“约会”，指人人安排却无人守约的那一次而不是别的，是一个夏天里人人都安排、却无人守约的东西。
date 意为“日期”，指日历上写到、被圈出的那一个，到 1966 年这个日期成了日历里的一行。
date 意为“日期、时日”，办事员三月写道，整件事的时日是一本登记簿和十个星期的确定。
date 意为“约会”，我记得的是末尾那一次，1978 年赴约，至今仍被说成登记簿上最奇的一次。
date 为抽象总称，姑姑 1980 年说，一个约会是唯一会因为被赴约而变得更好的东西。
